findings.area: Flip bloom in 112 COOL THE VOLCANO on phone: the finish-card prediction is wrong, so all three words fade almost at once (a regression from the interaction with the volcano round-1 fix)
findings.evidence:
Status of the round-1 findings, checked on scratch build /tmp/eos_rev_mood_code_int (mood, dots, 111-114). These are FIXED:
- No game-content overlap at 700 ms or 1300 ms for 111, 112 and 113 at 390, 114 at 1280, POP and 109 at 390. My own test also counts SVG, canvas and emoji (/tmp/rev_mood_c2/r_*.json).
- The bloom is 1500 ms + 0/200/400 ms delays, read through getTiming (eosMoodRise and eosMoodFade), so it ends at 1.9 s, inside the 2.05 s hold.
- Text is measured at weight 900.
- The HUD carve works. HUD luminance with the mood layers vs without: 43/42 vs 41/42, 44/42 vs 40/42, 36/39 vs 36/38.
- For legacy press cards the prediction lands within 3 px (game 2: guess y 319, real y 322).
- moves is always 0, with no page errors or warnings.

NEW PROBLEM: predictCard (lines 783-802) assumes the card is centred in .cinematicContentShell for every id of 100 or more. Commit f09a89f, which came after this module's fix, moved 112's card in 22_eos_game_volcano.jsx: line 1389 sets `:has(>.eosG112)>.globalFinishFeedbackCopy{top:var(--eosVolcFinY,66%)!important}`, and line 447 sets it to pipsY+20 on phone.

When isComplete arrives before the card (seen in 3 of 4 phone runs), at 390x844:
- The guess is {x:10,y:265,w:340,h:128} but the real card is {x:10,y:371,w:340,h:121}, about 103 px lower.
- eosMoodPlace pushes the crown below the guess, into the card's real slot: anchor (223,481), tight layout.
- follow() then makes every word yield, and place.yields becomes 3.
- The card shows about 450 ms after the bloom (p112.json). The words fade at about 0.5-1.1 s, so the third word ('strong', starting at 400 ms) yields almost as soon as it appears.
- Evidence: /tmp/rev_mood_c2/rm112.json and r_112_390.json (all three words have isYield at the freeze).

When the card is already on screen at the finish (t112.json), the crown blooms correctly at the Still Point. So the payoff for the anger hero game on phone is lost about half the time or more, depending on timing.
findings.fix:
Predict the card from the real CSS instead of a hard-coded model. Options:
(a) For ids of 100 or more, build a hidden probe in the card's parent (the shell): a div with className 'globalFeedbackCopyLayer globalFinishFeedbackCopy', visibility:hidden, animation:none, and the same <b>/<span> lines. Measure it with eosRelRect, then remove it in the same task, so every game override such as :has(>.eosG112) applies.
(b) Add a small contract instead: hero engines that move the card publish its top, either as a CSS var such as --eos-finish-card-y or as a data attribute on the host, and predictCard reads it. The volcano already sets --eosVolcFinY on the host, so read that too until it adopts the contract.
Add a regression case to overlap.mjs for 112 at 390x844 with the card arriving after isComplete, asserting yields 0 (or at most 1).

findings.area: Placement cost of a crowded finish (runs synchronously on the finish frame)
findings.evidence:
fire() runs inside the MutationObserver callback in the same task that paints isComplete. When no clean spot exists, eosMoodPlace (lines 359-407) works through every tier: about 63 + 234 + 468 + 1404 (about 2,200) candidates, each checking 3 boxes against every obstacle. That is the normal path for 113 GROUND CONTROL at 390, which always ends at tier 3 / stack.

Measured with window.__eos.mood.place on a synthetic 360x658 stage at 4x CPU throttle:
- 60 obstacles: 9 ms
- 120 obstacles: 31 ms
- 300 obstacles: 39-57 ms

The content scan allows up to 80 pictures + 220 text lines + chrome (/tmp/rev_mood_c2/perf2.mjs). The builder's 10-13 ms only holds for lighter stages, so a low-end phone can drop frames at the finish moment. The per-tick content scan in follow() is cheap: 0.4-2 ms at 1x, up to 7 ms at 4x on HAMMER.
findings.fix:
Use any of these:
- Pre-filter the obstacles once per tier or font size to those inside the band the grid can reach.
- Merge the text-line rects of one element into one box.
- Stop scoring a candidate as soon as its running score passes the best so far.
- Use a coarser y step (36 px) in tier 3.

findings.area: Card prediction is wrong for 112 COOL THE VOLCANO at phone size, so the finish card covers the flip words (round-1 finding 6 is back after a later integration change)
findings.evidence: predictCard (lines 783-802) assumes the finish card for ids 100 and up is centred in .cinematicContentShell. At 390 that gives a guess of {x:10,y:265,w:340,h:128} in root px, card centre at viewport y 392. The volcano round-1 fix (commit f09a89f, 05:37) landed after the mood fix (259e56b, 04:59). It moves the 112 card with `:has(>.eosG112)>.globalFinishFeedbackCopy{top:var(--eosVolcFinY,66%)!important}` (src/eos/22_eos_game_volcano.jsx:1389, var set at :447 to pipsY+20 on phone). The real card is therefore centred at y 495-506. In both runs of /tmp/rev_mood_r2/card.mjs (c112a.json, c112b.json), placement used the guess (card not yet present, tier 2 'tight'). The words were put just below the predicted band, with word centres at viewport y 504-533. The card arrived 898 ms and 1760 ms after the bloom, measured 700 ms into its entrance at [129,468,132,54], and landed on them. In the screenshots taken with each word frozen 700 ms in (/tmp/rev_mood_r2/v112c_a.png, v112c_b.png), no word is visible because the 'RELEASED ✓' and 'LIGHTER ✓' card (z 1200) covers all three. When the card already exists at fire time, placement is correct: run p112 put a clean crown around the Still Point. Desktop 112 is unaffected. Effect: in the anger hero game on phone, the cool / clear / strong bloom is cut short, either hidden by the card or yielding (fading) 0.4-1.7 s in.
findings.fix: Do not hard-code the card position per wrapper. Measure where the arcade CSS plus the game's CSS will actually put the card. For one measure in fire(), insert a hidden probe `<div class="globalFinishFeedbackCopy" style="visibility:hidden">` with a two-line body into the same parent the arcade uses (.cinematicContentShell's .globalFeedbackCopyLayer), read its rect and remove it. This picks up any per-game override such as 112's --eosVolcFinY. As a fallback, honour an optional `data-eos-card-y` set by game owners. Add 112 at 390, with the card arriving after the bloom, to the overlap acceptance test.

findings.area: In the crowded 113 GROUND CONTROL finale at phone size, the stacked words still partly cover the game's own emoji anchors
findings.evidence: eosMoodContent (lines 471-475) skips every text node with fewer than 2 letters, to ignore emoji particles and '+10'. In 113 the finale's constellation anchors, the 'found' things joined to the hero by golden lines (span inside .eosGroundFound, about 23 px), are pure emoji. They are therefore invisible to placement. Measured at 113 anxiety, 390, normal motion, with each word frozen 700 ms in (/tmp/rev_mood_r2/emo113.mjs, screenshot /tmp/rev_mood_r2/emo113.png): placement fell to tier 3 'stack' at 21 px. The words sit on the left anchor column: 'steady' covers 20 % of 🟡 and 7 % of 🖐️, 'here' 18 % of 🖐️, 'okay' 33 % of 👣. It looks cluttered against the finale's constellation. The reduced-motion run of the same game placed a clean crown between the HUD and the 'Touchdown' headline (/tmp/rev_mood_r2/v112c_r113.png), so a clean spot exists when these anchors are counted.
findings.fix: Count static pictographic glyphs (\p{Extended_Pictographic}) whose rendered box is 18 px or more as hard 'img' obstacles. To keep particles excluded, skip elements with running animations or inside particle containers. Also ask the 113 owner to tag .eosGroundFound (and the character) with data-eos-avoid, and add an emoji-anchor check to overlap.mjs.

findings.area: Placement runs synchronously on the frame where the game's finale starts
findings.evidence: fire() runs inside the isComplete MutationObserver callback (lines 933-938). It does the content scan (eosMoodContent, 1-5 ms) and the full tiered search (eosMoodPlace, lines 359-407) in one task. Measured on this server CPU (/tmp/rev_mood_r2/perf.mjs and iso.mjs): 6-23 ms for the crowded 113 phone finale (falls through to tier 3), and 27 ms for a synthetic busy stage with 250 obstacles. A mid-range phone runs JS 3-5x slower, so expect a 30-120 ms stall exactly when the game's own finale burst begins. follow() repeats the content scan every 120 ms for 1.9 s.
findings.fix: Keep the result identical but move it off the critical frame. Options: (a) cull the obstacles once per tier to those that intersect the grid's bounding box; (b) stop as soon as a clean candidate scores within the distance cost of the best possible; (c) run fire() in the next requestAnimationFrame (a one-frame delay is invisible), or pre-compute the chrome and grid geometry at 90 % progress so only the final hard-obstacle pass runs at isComplete.
